sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The tourism index is measured by international tourist arrivals and ________. (b) Among all the monuments, the Taj Mahal, the Agra Fort and ________ are the most popular tourist sites.
questions.answer: (a) Tourism receipts. (b) Qutub Minar.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Tourist arrivals means the number of persons who get accommodation at a tourist centre for at least 48 hours. (b) Foreign tourist arrivals in India are measured with tourism receipts as the other main index.
questions.answer: (a) False: the stay is at least 24 hours. (b) True: the two main measures are arrivals and receipts.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Tourism is a smokeless industry with a unique quality of earning ________ exchange. (b) On 14 May ________ the Government of India declared the Ministry of Tourism a separate ministry.
questions.answer: (a) Foreign. (b) 2000.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) About two-thirds of domestic tourists are contributed by five states: Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh. (b) The number of foreign tourists arriving in India is continuously increasing.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) True (with small falls in some years).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The foreign exchange earnings during January–April 2013 were US$ 6.878 billion and in the same period of 2012 US$ ________ billion. (b) India captures more than half of the tourist arrivals and about ________ of the tourist receipts of South Asia.
Identify True or False. (a) Foreign tourist arrivals in India are continuously decreasing. (b) Tourism is a smokeless industry with a unique quality of earning foreign exchange.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The ranking of India in world tourism improved from 38th position (2011) to ________ in 2015. (b) India is a major tourist destination among the ________ nations.
questions.answer: (a) 24th. (b) South Asian.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) India is a major tourist destination among the South Asian nations. (b) Tourism in India has not grown substantially since the beginning of the 1990s.
questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: it has grown substantially.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) Diplomats posted in a foreign country are called tourists. (b) India is a country known for its friendly treatment to all visitors.
questions.answer: (a) False. (b) True.

questions.q: Identify True or False. (a) In 2014 the country from which India received the largest number of foreign tourists was the UK. (b) The share of foreign tourists in India is less than 1% of world tourists.
questions.answer: (a) False: it was the USA. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Sustainable tourism includes the minimum impact of tourist activities on ________. (b) Tourism is a fast-emerging sector particularly after the ________ of the Indian economy since 1991.
questions.answer: (a) The environment. (b) Liberalisation.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) 'Atithi Devo Bhava' means ________. (b) Tourism that involves interaction of tourists with local people and their cultural life is called ________ tourism.
questions.answer: (a) Guest is God. (b) Rural.

questions.q: True or False. (a) In India tourism is the largest industry. (b) About ten million people are employed directly or indirectly in tourism.
questions.answer: (a) False: the lesson calls it the third largest. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) The lowest decadal growth of foreign tourists between 1951 and 2010 was in 1980–90 at about ________ per cent. (b) The Mohammad Yunus committee was formed in ________.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Why did travel and tourism increase in recent decades in India? Explain any two reasons.
questions.answer: Rich countries' tourists had better finances and more leisure time for holidays and business trips. Better transport, accessibility, communication and accommodation also encouraged travel.

or.q: Explain spiritual tourism as an emerging dimension in India in two points.
or.answer: India is the confluence of Hinduism, Sikhism, Islam, Christianity, Buddhism and Jainism. Temples, mosques, monasteries and churches attract a huge number of domestic and international tourists.

questions.q: 'The trend of international tourist arrivals is almost continuously on the rise.' Support the statement with two arguments.
questions.answer: Arrivals rose from 16,829 in 1951 to 6.3 million in 2011 and 23.33 million in 2015. Only a few years such as 2001, 2002, 2009 and 2012 saw small falls.

questions.q: Describe any two features of a domestic tourist.
questions.answer: A domestic tourist travels within the country to a place other than the usual residence or work. The person stays in accommodation for at least 24 hours for leisure, pilgrimage, sports, health or study.

questions.q: Mention any two measures to boost tourism.
questions.answer: Government can give subsidies, packages and a liberal visa policy. Better infrastructure, safety and security and promotional shows abroad attract tourists.

questions.q: Differentiate between a domestic and an international tourist.
questions.answer: A domestic tourist travels within his own country and stays at least 24 hours away from home. An international tourist visits another country on a foreign passport and stays at least 24 hours without a paid job.

questions.q: Write a short note on MICE tourism.
questions.answer: MICE means Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions. It has grown fast since the economic liberalisation of 1991 and India has the infrastructure for business tourists.

questions.q: Explain the term 'health tourism'.
questions.answer: It is tourism for medical treatment, offering world-class treatment at low cost in ayurveda, naturopathy, unani, siddha and allopathy. It attracts patients from the US, Europe and the Middle East.

questions.q: What is meant by growth of tourism? State its two types.
questions.answer: Growth of tourism is the change in the number of tourists. Positive growth means more tourists than before and negative growth means fewer.

questions.q: Give two reasons for the growth of domestic tourism in India.
questions.answer: Rising income levels and purchasing power have grown. The emergence of a dynamic middle class has pushed domestic travel.

questions.q: Which are the top three states in domestic tourists in 2015? Name them.
questions.answer: Tamil Nadu (23.3%), Uttar Pradesh (14.3%) and Andhra Pradesh (8.4%).

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: 'The spatial distribution of tourism is a function of various environmental conditions.' Support the statement with three arguments.
questions.answer: (i) Climate sends plains tourists to hill stations in summer and cold-area tourists to warm places in winter. (ii) Landscape and geographical diversity (mountains, coasts, deserts) attract tourists to particular regions. (iii) Location and natural attractions decide the share of states: the top ten states get about 85% of domestic tourists.

questions.q: Explain any three features of health tourism.
questions.answer: (i) It offers world-class treatment at low cost. (ii) It includes the Indian systems of medicine such as ayurveda, naturopathy, unani and siddha along with allopathy. (iii) It attracts patients from the US, Europe and the Middle East where treatment is costly.

questions.q: Explain the concept of sustainable tourism in three points.
questions.answer: (i) It meets the needs of the present without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs. (ii) It keeps the impact of tourist activity on the environment to a minimum. (iii) It balances economic, social and environmental needs.

questions.q: Describe the pattern of foreign tourist arrivals in India (three points).
questions.answer: (i) In 2014 the USA (14.57%), Bangladesh (12.27%) and the UK (10.92%) were the top source countries. (ii) The top ten countries gave about 61.5% of the arrivals. (iii) Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Delhi received most foreign tourists and tourists stay a little over a month.

questions.q: Explain any three government initiatives for the promotion of tourism.
questions.answer: (i) A separate Tourism Department (1957), the Tourism Development Council (1958) and a Ministry of Tourism (2000). (ii) National Policy 1982, industry status in 1985–90, the Yunus Committee in 1988 and the National Action Plan in 1992. (iii) Incredible India campaign and simplified approvals for tour operators.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain any six factors affecting the growth of tourism.
questions.answer: (i) Geographical: climate, landscape and location decide the seasons and flows. (ii) Cultural events such as Durga Puja, Onam and Surajkund Mela attract crowds. (iii) Safety and security: tragedies reduce arrivals, as in Kashmir after 1985. (iv) Economic conditions: high-income people travel more. (v) Facilities and services: accommodation, transport, banking and guides. (vi) Government policies: subsidies, packages and a liberal visa policy.

questions.q: Explain six points of the emerging dimensions of Indian tourism.
questions.answer: (i) Health tourism offers low-cost world-class treatment. (ii) Spiritual tourism draws pilgrims to temples, mosques, churches and monasteries. (iii) Adventure tourism grows in high-altitude areas. (iv) MICE tourism has grown since 1991 with improved facilities. (v) Rural tourism lets tourists interact with local people and culture. (vi) Sustainable tourism minimises the impact on the environment.

questions.q: Discuss the growth and patterns of foreign and domestic tourists in India, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) FTAs rose from 16,829 in 1951 to 23.33 million in 2015. (ii) India's rank improved from 54th (2002) to 38th (2011) and 24th (2015), but its share stays below 1%. (iii) The USA, Bangladesh and the UK send the most; Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra receive the most foreign visitors. (iv) Domestic tourists grew from 159.88 million (1997) to 1,431.97 million (2015). (v) Tamil Nadu (23.3%) and Uttar Pradesh lead; five states give about 63% of domestic visits. (vi) FEEs were US$ 16.56 billion in 2011 and the government supports growth through the Ministry of Tourism.
